raw_case_text:
At 6-month-old baby girl, born to non-consanguineous parents of Swedish descent (Caucasians), was admitted to a Swedish hospital due to severe pneumonia. Previous medical records showed failure-to-thrive and thrombocytosis. She received respiratory support, corticosteroids, and antibiotics at the intensive care unit. Rhino- and bocavirus were detected in nasal swabs, and radiology suggested a bacterial infection. Due to halting recovery after a week, extended testing was performed, revealing unmeasurable immunoglobulin levels and a nasopharyngeal swab PCR positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii (PCJ). Radiology and further microbiologic testing confirmed PCJ pneumonia. This raised a suspicion of SCID, and antimicrobial therapy was adjusted and intravenous immunoglobulin substitution initiated. The patient was transferred to a tertiary pediatric hospital for intensive care and immunologic workup and treatment. Candida parapsiolosis was found in the feces. The necessity of allogenic HCT was evident; thus, it was carried out. The timeline is depicted in  Figure 1 .
Upon clinical diagnosis, we retrieved the patient's NBS sample and ran an SCID NBS assay analyzing both TRECs and KRECs: the TREC copy number was 110 copies/well [recall threshold <=5, population mean 79, IQR 55, 110 ] and KRECs were not measurable. Lymphocyte phenotyping in peripheral blood showed prevalent T lymphocytes of which the majority were CD4+ T lymphocytes, with a smaller fraction of CD8+ T lymphocytes. Both CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes had a uniform, atypical surface phenotype expressing intermediate levels of the naive cell marker CD45RA but high levels of the recent thymic emigrant marker CD31 ( Table 1 ). Analysis of the T lymphocyte receptor (TCR) Vbeta repertoire by flow cytometry revealed an essentially normal distribution in both CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, but an elevated level of CD4+ Vbeta2+ T lymphocytes (19%, upper normal limit 13%). B lymphocytes were severely reduced in numbers (0.02 x 109/L) and were all found to be naive (93% with no plasmablasts and switched memory cells,  Table 1 ). No specific antibodies to previous vaccinations were detected. Lymphocyte proliferation showed adequate response to mitogens, except for pokeweed mitogen (PWM) in B lymphocytes and concavalin A (ConA) in CD8+ T lymphocytes. Conversely, a lymphocyte response was not evoked to either tetanus or pneumococcus despite previous vaccinations, or candida despite positive cultures ( Table 1 ). Assessment of the myeloid compartment (e.g., erythro-, mono-, and neutrophil granulocytes) was normal, besides absent eosinophil granulocytes and thrombocytosis ( Table 1 ). Whole genome sequencing with an in silico filter for IEI showed a heterozygous sequence variant in IKZF1 (c.476A>G, p.Asn159Ser). Confirmatory Sanger sequencing of the patient and parents showed the mutation to be de novo.
At 10 months of age, our patient underwent allogeneic HCT with an unrelated 10/10 HLA-matched donor, the timeline is depicted in  Figure 1 . The PCJ pneumonia and respiratory viruses were cleared before admission. HCT conditioning consisted of fludarabine, treosulfan, and anti-thymocyte globulin. The HCT was performed with neutrophil and thrombocyte engraftment at days +36 and +24, respectively, without complications. Ciclosporin A and methotrexate were used as graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis. Six weeks after the procedure, cutaneous and gastrointestinal GVHD grade 1 occurred and was treated with prednisolone. Thereafter, CMV viremia occurred, with good response to pre-emptive therapy with valganciclovir. Because of mixed chimerism with low counts of T and B lymphocytes, an evaluating bone marrow biopsy was performed approximately +4 months post-HCT. It revealed near total CD34+ autologous reconstitution, i.e., graft failure/rejection. Hence, re-HCT was performed with repeated conditioning (i.e., same as in first HCT with the addition of thiotepa) and the same donor and GVHD prophylaxis. Neutrophil and thrombocyte engraftment were seen at days +19 and +20, respectively. The re-HCT was without significant complications.
Six months after re-HCT, the patient displayed full donor chimerism. An additional 12 months later, our patient experienced several uncomplicated upper airway infections, with spontaneous recovery. Twenty-seven months after re-HCT, the patient is alive and well, without any continuous treatment. She has a full numeric immune recovery (lymphocytes and immunoglobulins), responded adequately to vaccinations, is developing as expected, and is now in preschool.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 6-month-old Caucasian female infant of Swedish descent was admitted with severe pneumonia and a prior history of failure to thrive.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The infant was admitted at 6 months of age to a Swedish hospital with severe pneumonia requiring intensive care unit respiratory support, corticosteroids, and empiric antibiotics. Initial nasal swabs detected rhinovirus and bocavirus, and chest imaging suggested bacterial pneumonia, but her clinical recovery halted after 1 week of therapy, prompting an extended immunological and microbiological evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Failure to thrive and persistent thrombocytosis documented in prior medical records; born to non-consanguineous Caucasian parents of Swedish descent; previously immunized according to schedule.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe respiratory distress/pneumonia and failure to thrive.

objective.physical_examination: Severe pneumonia requiring pediatric ICU respiratory support; failure to thrive.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial microbiology: Nasal swabs positive for rhinovirus and bocavirus; fecal culture positive for Candida parapsilosis. Extended baseline immunology and hematology: Unmeasurable serum immunoglobulin levels and complete absence of specific antibodies to prior vaccinations (tetanus, pneumococcus); normal myeloid compartment (erythrocytes, monocytes, neutrophils) except for absent eosinophils and persistent thrombocytosis.
objective.advanced_workup: Opportunistic pathogen testing: Nasopharyngeal swab PCR and confirmatory microbiological/radiological testing positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii (PCJ) pneumonia. Newborn screening (NBS) card retrospective SCID assay: Normal TREC copy number at 110 copies/well (recall threshold <=5, population mean 79) but unmeasurable KRECs. Peripheral blood lymphocyte phenotyping and function: Prevalent T cells (predominantly CD4+ over CD8+) with a uniform atypical surface phenotype expressing intermediate CD45RA and high CD31 (recent thymic emigrants); TCR Vbeta repertoire largely normal except elevated CD4+ Vbeta2+ T cells (19%, upper normal limit 13%); severely reduced B lymphocytes (0.02 x 10^9/L), 93% naive without plasmablasts or switched memory B cells; impaired lymphocyte proliferation to pokeweed mitogen (PWM) in B cells, concanavalin A (ConA) in CD8+ T cells, and specific antigens (tetanus, pneumococcus, Candida). Whole-genome sequencing (IEI filter) and confirmatory trio Sanger sequencing: Identified a de novo heterozygous missense mutation in IKZF1, c.476A>G (p.Asn159Ser).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCJ, confirmed by nasopharyngeal swab PCR and radiology) and severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) caused by a de novo heterozygous IKZF1 mutation (c.476A>G, p.Asn159Ser), accompanied by rhinovirus/bocavirus co-infection and fecal Candida parapsilosis colonization. Plan and clinical course: Treated in the tertiary pediatric ICU with targeted anti-Pneumocystis antimicrobial therapy and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) replacement, clearing PCJ pneumonia and respiratory viruses prior to transplantation. At 10 months of age, she underwent allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) from a 10/10 HLA-matched unrelated donor (conditioned with fludarabine, treosulfan, and anti-thymocyte globulin; GVHD prophylaxis with cyclosporine A and methotrexate), complicated by grade 1 cutaneous/GI GVHD (treated with prednisolone), CMV viremia (treated with valganciclovir), and autologous CD34+ graft rejection at +4 months. A second HCT using the same donor with added thiotepa conditioning achieved neutrophil/platelet engraftment by days +19/+20 and full donor chimerism at 6 months. At 27 months post-re-HCT, she is alive and well off all therapy with full numerical and functional immune reconstitution.
